profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting at a mid-sized asset management firm evaluating whether an internal research proposal can move from research prototype to pilot deployment in the firm's discretionary-quant equities sleeve. The proposal describes a deep-learning-based daily stock trading system using a novel return-weighted loss function trained on public OHLCV, sector labels, and technical indicators, with reported backtest results from 2005-2010 and 2019-2024. The meeting agenda is to review whether the design is sufficiently complete for pilot approval, identify any changes needed in the model card and implementation plan, and confirm what evidence will be presented to the model risk committee next week. The expected outcome is a conditional approval to proceed, with both participants believing they have aligned on what 'pilot-ready' means and what revisions are needed before submission.

members.name: Lena Park
members.expertise: Deep learning for equities, backtesting methodology, factor-neutral portfolio construction
members.background: Former academic ML researcher who joined the firm's systematic equities team three years ago and now translates research ideas into internal model proposals.
members.private_state: Wants the proposal to pass design review with minimal rework so her team can secure compute budget and begin a live shadow run this quarter; she is especially concerned that extra documentation requests could delay committee submission.
hidden_assumptions: If a design is 'pilot-ready,' it means the research logic, offline backtest evidence, and portfolio simulation are stable enough for a paper-trading shadow deployment, even if some production controls are still handled by existing desk processes.

The reported daily rebalancing results already reflect realistic implementation because her team's standard backtest template includes next-day execution after end-of-day signal generation and their default slippage settings.

The 'risk review pack' for a research design review mainly needs aggregate performance, turnover, drawdown, and a concise ablation of the novel loss function, because committee members usually ask for those artifacts first.
When discussing the '2019-2024 test period,' everyone means the post-tuning out-of-sample window used in the current draft, not every modern-era experiment run during development.

members.name: Marcus Feld
members.expertise: Model governance, validation standards, trading system controls, implementation risk assessment
members.background: Previously worked in prime brokerage risk oversight and now reviews quantitative strategies before they can be used in any client-facing or internal investment process.
members.private_state: Wants to avoid approving something that later fails committee scrutiny or creates an unlogged implementation gap; he prefers to keep the review constructive and not appear obstructive to the research team.
hidden_assumptions: If a design is 'pilot-ready,' it means the package is ready for a governed limited-production pilot with explicit execution assumptions, monitoring thresholds, exception handling, and reproducible validation artifacts.

A claim of 'daily rebalancing' in a trading proposal ordinarily implies same-day operational readiness has been translated into a documented order-generation and execution workflow, not just a research backtest convention.

The 'risk review pack' should include distributional breakdowns, implementation sensitivity, and replay-ready experiment lineage because aggregate charts alone are not sufficient for approval decisions.

When someone refers to the '2019-2024 test period,' that usually includes the full recent-market holdout evidence that would be shown to committee, including the final stress months and the exact frozen model version.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the design should be 'pilot-ready' before committee submission.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'pilot-ready' means ready for a shadow or paper-trading pilot based on stable research evidence, while relying on existing desk controls for operational details.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'pilot-ready' means ready for a governed limited-production pilot package with explicit control documentation, monitoring, and validation artifacts.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both commonly use the same internal phrase and both support moving forward, so the apparent agreement masks that they are applying different readiness thresholds rather than openly disagreeing.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as daily rebalancing implementation
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss whether the 'daily rebalancing setup' is already reflected in the design.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means her standard research workflow: generate signals after market close using public data and simulate fills at the next day's open with house-default slippage.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means the design has an explicitly documented operational procedure for daily order generation, cutoffs, stale-data handling, and executable trade timing for the pilot.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds operationally complete to both, but each is filling in the missing method from their own team's default process, so neither feels a need to unpack the exact execution mechanics.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of the risk review pack
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to tighten the 'risk review pack' before sending materials onward.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the pack is the research-facing design appendix: top-line performance tables, turnover, drawdowns, a comparison against baseline losses, and a brief note on feature limitations.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the pack extends to governance artifacts: scenario breakdowns, sensitivity to transaction cost shifts, frozen-code lineage, and alert thresholds for live monitoring.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see themselves as discussing one familiar document, but each treats a different layer of artifacts as obviously included, and the term 'pack' is broad enough to preserve false consensus.

misalignment_points.topic: Reference set behind the modern test window
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to 'the 2019-2024 test period' as support for the proposal's robustness.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the 1,340-day out-of-sample window reported in the draft after the final tuning lock, excluding a few discarded experimental runs and not emphasizing the exact freeze lineage.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the full recent-era holdout evidence that should map exactly to the final frozen model package presented to committee, including the stress months and experiment traceability.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both cite the same date range and believe they are referencing the same evidence block, but one thinks in terms of the polished result table and the other thinks in terms of the auditable validation dataset tied to the final version.

turns.inner_thought: I need to frame this as ready to move with only light edits. The core research is done: the return-weighted loss is the real contribution, the public-data-only feature set keeps it clean, and the backtests are stable enough for a shadow deployment. If I present it as pilot-ready in the normal research sense, we should be able to get through design review and secure compute without inviting a long operational documentation cycle.
turns.utterance: At a high level, the proposal is pretty straightforward: a deep-learning equity signal trained on public OHLCV, sector labels, and technical indicators, with the return-weighted loss improving the ranking quality versus the standard objectives we tried. The backtest profile is strong across the long history and the recent window, and from my perspective the design is pilot-ready.

turns.inner_thought: I like the direction, but I need to make sure 'pilot-ready' means the committee won't immediately ask where the controls, monitoring, and validation lineage are. I don't want to sound like I'm blocking research, so better to position this as confirming what still needs to be in place before next week.
turns.utterance: I generally like the direction as well. Before we use that label with the committee, I just want to confirm what you see as needing to be in place for it to be pilot-ready for next week's review.

turns.inner_thought: He probably just wants the standard design-review framing. The daily rebalancing setup is already in the research template: signals at end of day, next-session execution, default slippage. That's representative enough for this stage. And the risk review pack should just summarize the key performance and model evidence so we can avoid getting dragged into a giant appendix rewrite.
turns.utterance: From the research side, the daily rebalancing setup is already reflected in the design, so I don't think we're missing anything fundamental there. For the review materials, I was planning to keep the risk review pack focused on the current evidence set and make sure it's tight enough to support the submission.

turns.inner_thought: Good, if the daily rebalancing setup is already covered, then maybe this is mostly a packaging issue. I still need the operating assumptions, monitoring logic, and implementation framing to show up clearly in the pack, but I can ask for that gently without reopening the whole design.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. If the daily rebalancing setup is already reflected in the design, then what I'd want is for the operating assumptions to come through cleanly in the risk review pack alongside the usual evidence.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect, he's asking for presentation cleanup, not a new workstream. I can tighten the pack around the metrics committee usually asks for first: returns, Sharpe, turnover, drawdown, and the ablation showing the loss function matters. That's manageable and won't delay submission.
turns.utterance: Yes, that's reasonable. We can tighten the risk review pack around the headline return profile, Sharpe, turnover, drawdown, and the ablation showing the return-weighted loss outperforming the standard objectives. That should make the core case much clearer.

turns.inner_thought: Those top-line items are fine as a start. I also need confidence that the recent holdout being cited is the exact evidence tied to the frozen version we'd present. If the 2019-2024 test period is the final package window, that gives me a basis to say the robustness story is anchored properly.
turns.utterance: That sounds good. I think the 2019-2024 test period should be enough to support robustness, as long as that's the one tied to the final package.

turns.inner_thought: He's referring to the recent out-of-sample block in the draft, which is exactly what I planned to show. That window already captures the relevant modern volatility regimes and is the polished evidence set. No need to revisit every developmental run as long as the draft table is in good shape.
turns.utterance: Agreed. The 2019-2024 test period in the draft already captures the more recent volatility and is the right main validation window for the proposal.

turns.inner_thought: I should nudge for implementation sensitivity without sounding like I'm demanding a full rebuild. If the committee sees a short section showing the daily rebalancing design has been thought through beyond pure research results, it'll be much easier to defend this as pilot-ready.
turns.utterance: One thing I'd add is a short section on implementation sensitivity. That would help the committee see the daily rebalancing setup as fully thought through rather than purely academic, and it would strengthen the case that this is pilot-ready.

turns.inner_thought: I can live with a short appendix addition if it keeps this moving. The key is not letting this turn into a request to redesign the workflow. The model is done; this is just packaging around the edges, and we can expand the risk review pack without changing the substance.
turns.utterance: That's reasonable. We can expand the appendix and tighten the risk review pack a bit without changing the core design, because the model itself is effectively complete.

turns.inner_thought: Good. With the pack updated and the recent evidence attached, I can support this going forward. I believe we're converging on a governed pilot submission, and I'd rather keep momentum than create friction now as long as those materials show up in the bundle.
turns.utterance: Great. In that case, I'm comfortable positioning this as pilot-ready once the risk review pack is updated and the 2019-2024 evidence is attached in the submission bundle.
